He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]] and [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington Huskies]]. ==Early life and high school== Tucker grew up in [[Bowie, Maryland]] and initially attended [[Mount Saint Joseph High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2021/08/18/mount-saint-josephs-bryson-tucker-named-to-usa-basketball-under-16-team-will-compete-in-fiba-americas-championship/|title=Mount Saint Joseph's Bryson Tucker named to USA Basketball Under-16 team, will compete in FIBA Americas Championship|work=[[Baltimore Sun]]|date=August 18, 2021|access-date=March 22, 2024}} He averaged 22.3 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 2.3 assists per game as a sophomore. Tucker transferred to [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]] before the start of his junior year.{{cite web|url=https://highschool.si.com/florida/2022/06/11/report-mount-st-josephs-baltimore-bryson-tucker-is-headed-south-to-img-academy|title=Report: Mount St. Joseph’s (Baltimore) Bryson Tucker is headed south to IMG Academy|first=Gary|last=Adornato|website=[[SI.com]]|date=June 12, 2022|access-date=March 22, 2024}} He left IMG midway through his junior season.{{cite web|url=https://www.thebaltimorebanner.com/sports/bryson-tucker-transfer-recruitment-michigan-state-duke-maryland-YF35T45CFJCUFE3QZUYU3LYVHI/|title=What's next for Baltimore basketball phenom Bryson five-star recruit and one of the top players in the 2024 class, according to major recruiting services.{{cite web|url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article281716053.html|title=Senior small forward prospect from high school in Virginia visiting Kansas Tucker|first=Corey|last=Robinson|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=October 16, 2023|access-date=March 22, 2024}} He committed to play college basketball at Indiana over offers from [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]], and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2024/04/01/iubb-what-mcdonalds-all-american-bryson-tucker-brings-to-iu-mike-woodson-recruiting-indiana-hoosiers/73163424007/|title=What McDonald's All American Bryson Tucker brings to IU basketball|work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=April 1, 2024|access-date=April 2, 2024}} Tucker also considered playing professionally in the [[NBA G League]] for [[NBA G League Ignite]] before it was announced that the program would be discontinued.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5375971/2024/03/28/bryson-tucker-indiana-recruit/|title=Indiana lands 5-star recruit Bryson Tucker: What’s next for the Hoosiers?|first=Tobias|last=Bass|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=March 28, 2024|access-date=April 2, 2024}} ==College career== Tucker averaged 5.4 points and 2.9 rebounds per game as a freshman at Indiana. Following the season he transferred to [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]].{{cite news |last1=Simms |first1=Brandy |title=Maryland native Bryson Tucker transfers to Washington |url=https://www.si.com/high-school/maryland/maryland-native-bryson-tucker-transfers-to-washington-01jv7n64txf4 |access-date=December 13, 2025 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=May 14, 2025}} On November 9, 2025, Tucker sprained his ankle in a 78-69 loss at [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]].{{cite news |last1=Raley |first1=Dan |title=Bryson Tucker Ruled Out Of Friday's Game at WSU |url=https://www.si.com/college/washington/basketball/bryson-tucker-ruled-out-of-friday-s-game-at-wsu-01k9x48djk75 |access-date=December 13, 2025 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=November 12, 2025}} ==National team career== Tucker played for the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States national under-16 team]] at the [[2021 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]]. He averaged 9.5 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 1.2 steals per game as the United States won the gold medal.{{cite web|url=https://www.maizenbrew.com/2023/1/23/23566395/michigan-wolverines-basketball-recruiting-2024-class-five-star-bryson-tucker-offer|title=Michigan extends offer to 2024 five-star small forward Bryson Tucker|first=Kellen|last=Voss|website=MaizeNBrew.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=January 23, 2023|access-date=March 26, 2024}} ==Personal== Tucker's father Byron played collegiately for NC State and George Mason from 1988 to 1992.{{cite web |title=Men’s Basketball Signs Bryson Tucker |url=https://iuhoosiers.com/news/2024/4/18/mens-basketball-mens-basketball-signs-bryson-tucker |website=Indiana University Athletics |publisher=Indiana University |access-date=28 June 2024 |language=en |date=18 April 2024}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[https://iuhoosiers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/bryson-tucker/18779 Indiana Hoosiers bio] *[https://gohuskies.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/bryson-tucker/17112 Washington Huskies bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Tucker, Bryson}} [[Category:2006 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Maryland]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Small forwards]] [[Category:Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball players]] [[Category:Washington Huskies men's basketball players]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]]
